plan_version: LW-WATCHTOWER v0.3.0 - the release plan for THIS PROJECT, not for the repository you are working in
_why_this_file_exists: This is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for /lw-watchtower:checklist, and it is a TRACKED file in the repo
rather than the plan file it was transcribed from. Three candidates were considered.
The plan file lives at a per-machine path under ~/.claude/plans, is not tracked, and ships
with nothing - so on any other machine the command would report an empty plan or refuse to
run, and its checkboxes are hand-ticked, which is precisely the evidence-free claim this
plugin exists to catch. The session task list is ephemeral, unreachable from a script, and
carries no evidence at all. A tracked file is reviewable in a pull request, versioned with
the code it describes, ships with the plugin, and can carry a MACHINE-CHECKABLE evidence
rule per item - which is the only thing that lets a checkbox mean anything.
ITS STALENESS RISK, stated rather than disclaimed: this file is maintained by hand, so it
can drift from the plan in three ways. An item can be silently DELETED and vanish from the
report. A new plan item can be added and never transcribed here. And an evidence rule can be
written loose enough to pass without the work being done. The first two are measured on
every run by source_plan below - the command counts the plan's checkboxes and sections and
reports any that no item here covers - and that measurement is itself unavailable on a
machine without the plan file, where the command says so instead of passing quietly. The
third is not detectable by any automated means; it is why every DONE row prints the evidence
it rests on, so a reader can judge the rule rather than trust the tick.
AND THE MULTI-LAPTOP CONSEQUENCE, which the degradation above is careful about but does not
name: the plan lives under one user profile on one machine, so drift is measurable on EXACTLY
ONE laptop and on no other. Everywhere else the command correctly prints STALENESS NOT
MEASURED with the reason and never claims 'no drift' - but the honest report of a gap is not
the gap being closed. A plan item added and never transcribed here is undetectable from any
second machine, and the checklist there will look complete while being short an item. Do not
read a clean run on a laptop without the plan file as agreement between plan and checklist;
it is silence about whether they agree. The only fix is to transcribe on the machine that
holds the plan, or to track the plan.

source_plan.note: THE PLAN FILE NAME IS NO LONGER TRACKED, AND THE CAPABILITY IT SERVED DID NOT GO WITH IT - IT MOVED TO AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE. This field used to hold a literal path ending in the plan file own name, under one user profile. That file is untracked, ships with nothing and exists on exactly one machine - yet every consumer who installed this plugin received the name, because the whole repository root is the plugin payload and source ./ has no exclusion mechanism. Naming it told a stranger only that a maintainer personal plan exists and what it is called: disclosure with no reader it helps. So the literal is gone and path_env names an environment variable instead. Set LWG_SOURCE_PLAN to the plan path on the machine that actually holds it and drift is measured exactly as before; set nowhere - which is everywhere except that one machine - the run prints STALENESS NOT MEASURED with the reason, which is what it already printed on every other machine and is the honest answer rather than a silent pass. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, unchanged before and after: an untranscribed plan item is still undetectable from any machine without the plan, so a clean-looking checklist there is silence about plan agreement rather than evidence of it.

items.section: Phase 1 - Repo restructure to OSS best practice
items.title: Settle the CRLF-vs-LF disagreement in .gitattributes AND .editorconfig
items.caveat: THE PROBE WAS EXISTENCE-ONLY UNTIL 2026-08-03 AND THE TITLE IS ABOUT AGREEMENT. It named both files and read neither: Test-LwgEvidence opens a file only when `contains` or `not_contains` is set, so `Test-Path -PathType Leaf` twice was the entire proof of a row whose question is whether the contents of two files agree. Nothing was wrong at the time - the two files do agree, rule for rule - so the tick was correct for the wrong reason, which is the state this manifest is least able to notice. IT NOW PINS EXACTLY ONE RULE OF FOUR, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT IT CHECKS. The same pattern is applied to both paths, because the evidence schema carries one `contains` for the whole path set, and the two files are written in different syntaxes - so the pattern is the one line the two spell close enough to share: the statusline/statusline.ps1 LF pin, `text eol=lf` in .gitattributes and `end_of_line = lf` under a [statusline/statusline.ps1] section in .editorconfig. That rule was chosen over the other three because it is the one with a live consequence: docs/install.md records that the LF pin is what makes a fresh clone reproduce ~\.claude\statusline.ps1 byte for byte, so bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's Get-FileHash drift comparison keeps meaning something. Lose it from either file and that comparison starts reporting drift on every clone. WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT PROVE: that the two files agree. The default rule, the *.ps1 CRLF rule and the *.sh rule are unread, so any of them could be changed in one file and not the other with this row still green; and the pattern allows up to 120 characters between the path and the ending, so a reformat that moves them further apart defeats it and renders the row NOT STARTED - a false accusation, which is why the span is generous rather than tight. A probe that actually tested the title would have to extract (glob -> line-ending) pairs from both syntaxes and compare the sets. That is a tracked scanner with its own exit contract, in the shape of tests/portability_scan.ps1, and it is NOT what this row does.

items.section: Phase 2 - OSS-grade documentation (gate: complete BEFORE going public)
items.title: Split the 1000-line README into docs/: install, configuration, modules, architecture, troubleshooting, faq
items.caveat: THIS TICK RESTS ON SIX FILES EXISTING AND ON NOTHING ELSE. It flipped to DONE on 30 July 2026 when docs/faq.md landed - the sixth and last name in the list - and the probe did exactly one thing: confirmed six paths are readable files. It says NOTHING about whether the pages are any good, whether they are complete, whether they are consistent with each other, or whether a single sentence on any of them is still TRUE. That last one is not a nitpick: three pages were found stating the pre-gate, pre-test state as current on the day this item passed, and each was corrected by hand. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CHECKS THAT A SENTENCE IN docs/ IS STILL TRUE. tests/portability_scan.ps1 checks that no tracked file names a machine and bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's `commands` check catches a reference to a command that does not exist; between them that is the WHOLE of automated prose checking, and neither can see a claim that has gone stale. docs/limitations.md states this as a limitation in its own right. The README-split requirement is also only half of what the section heading asks for: 'complete BEFORE going public' is a judgement about the documentation set, and a file-existence probe cannot make one.

items.title: The owner's personal address appears on no commit of any BRANCH, and a default clone shows only LEAPWare-HQ <leapware@outlook.com>
items.caveat: REWRITTEN TWICE AND RESCOPED ONCE MORE ON 2026-07-31, AND ALL THREE CHANGES ARE RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN ONLY THE FLATTERING ONES. The third touched the TITLE and this caveat, not the probe - the evidence command is unchanged by it. First, by owner decision: the plan called for a GitHub noreply address and the owner explicitly chose leapware@outlook.com instead - a real, reachable address rather than a routing alias - which the rule's original consumer-domain ban would have failed forever. The rule was changed to state the decision; the decision was not changed to satisfy the rule. WHAT THE REWRITE ACTUALLY DID: 89 commits, every one reachable from every BRANCH, had author and committer rewritten through a mailmap by git-filter-repo 2.47.0; tree hashes, author dates and subjects came through byte-identical, so nothing but identity moved. All 14 branch heads were force-pushed the same day, and a fresh clone shows exactly one identity, LEAPWare-HQ <leapware@outlook.com>. SECOND, AND THIS IS THE PART A LATER READER NEEDS: the evidence used to assert that EVERY line of `git log --all --format=%ae%n%ce` was the chosen address, by way of a negative lookahead that tripped on any line that was not. That assertion is unsatisfiable in a living repository, and it was MEASURED so rather than predicted - Dependabot authored a commit on a PR branch on 2026-07-31, and `git log --all` spans remote-tracking refs, so a single fetched bot branch turned this row red while nothing whatever about the rewrite had regressed. That branch is gone, but .github/dependabot.yml schedules github-actions updates weekly, so the next run recreates the situation. The rule now asserts exactly what the rewrite promised and can keep: the owner's personal address appears on NO commit of ANY branch, and the chosen address is present. It deliberately does NOT claim that every commit is the owner's, because a repository that accepts bot-authored PR branches cannot hold that property, and a rule that goes red every week teaches people to ignore red rows - which is worse than not having the rule. THE NEGATIVE PATTERN IS NO LONGER SPELLED HERE, AND THE ARGUMENT THAT LET IT BE IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DELETED. It used to carry the local-part of the address in reading order, and the caveat argued that was safe because this probe reads the output of git log and never the working tree, so the manifest containing the string cannot make the probe pass falsely. That argument is CORRECT ABOUT THE PROBE and says nothing about PUBLICATION. On a public repository the local-part sits beside CHANGELOG.md's record that identities were rewritten to leapware@outlook.com and beside an open issue naming the surviving pull ref, and the three together hand a reader the whole former address - which a pre-publication audit measured as appearing in NO public repository today, so publishing it would be a first disclosure rather than a re-exposure. It also defeated the cleaning tools: a git filter-repo --replace-text pass matches a literal in reading order and walked straight past this one. The pattern is now stored rot13-encoded with a rot13: prefix and decoded by Expand-LwgRptLiteral in bin/lwg-evidence.ps1 at the moment it is applied; the ENCODED form is what any detail line prints, so the address no longer reaches the operator's screen either. Rot13 is a transposition and not secrecy - anyone can undo it in one line - and that is the right strength, because the requirement is that no tracked file spells the target in reading order, not that the target be hidden. THIRD, ON 2026-07-31 AFTER v0.3.0 WAS TAGGED: the scope word in this title is BRANCH and not REF, because final verification of the release found that ref was an overclaim. What the rewrite did cover is every commit reachable from every branch, and that part stands unchanged. What it could not cover is a ref that GitHub owns rather than this repository and that no push can reach; its ancestry still carries the pre-rewrite identities. That is why this probe passing is an honest statement about every ref a reader will actually have, and not about every ref that exists - and if that history is ever landed in a ref that git log --all reaches, THIS ROW WILL GO RED, which is the probe working correctly on the refs actually present rather than a regression. THE LOCATION OF THAT REF, ITS TIP COMMIT, THE NUMBER OF COMMITS INVOLVED AND THE COMMAND THAT RETRIEVES THEM WERE SPELLED OUT IN THIS CAVEAT UNTIL 2026-08-03, AND REMOVING THEM IS THE POINT OF THIS EDIT. checklist.json is tracked, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json declares source ./ with no exclusion mechanism, and commands/checklist.md instructs the model to print this command output verbatim - so that paragraph was rendered on the screen of every stranger who installed the plugin and ran the command, presented as a finding about their own repository. It turned a bounded exposure into a signposted one: it named where to look and exactly how. THE EXPOSURE IS UNCHANGED BY THIS EDIT - only the signposting is gone, and the location now lives in the issue that owns it, addressed to the people who can act on it. WHAT WAS ALSO REMOVED, AND IT WAS THE MORE DANGEROUS SENTENCE: this caveat used to assert that the exposure reached no further than whoever could already read the repository, on the grounds that it is not yet published. That was true when written and inverts the instant visibility flips - inside a file that is public by then, which a reader would have relied on to decide the exposure was contained at exactly the moment it stopped being. A claim whose truth turns on an event nobody re-reads the file after does not belong in a shipped file. RESOLVING THE EXPOSURE IS A PRECONDITION OF PUBLICATION AND NOT OF THIS ROW: the remedies are owner actions that nothing in this tree can take or attest to. P8-visibility declares that precondition without naming the location

items.title: No occurrence of the private sibling project's name in the tracked tree (git grep finds none, i.e. exits 1)
items.caveat: RENAMED ON 2026-07-31, AND THE RENAME IS THE POINT. The old id was the name itself with a P3- prefix; its title and its own git grep argument spelled the name it required to be absent, so as long as checklist.json was tracked the rule guaranteed its own failure - a check that could never pass, sitting in this project's own evidence manifest. Two fixes were rejected before that one. Excluding checklist.json with a pathspec would have made the row pass while leaving the name plainly readable in a tracked file, which is worse than a red row. Splitting the literal across a concatenation is not available in JSON. THE BRACKET CLASS THAT REPLACED IT WAS ITSELF REPLACED ON 2026-08-03, AND THE ARGUMENT FOR IT WAS WRONG IN A WAY WORTH RECORDING. This caveat said the construction 'spells no matching literal'. True of git grep, and false of everything else that reads a file: a human, a search engine, an indexer or a language model reads a construction of that shape - written [Ff][Oo][Oo]... here, with the letters neutralised for the reason at the end of this caveat - left to right in about two seconds. It was the only occurrence of the name in the tip tree, it sat inside the row whose job is to assert the name is absent, and /lw-watchtower:checklist PRINTED it in that row's detail line on every machine that ran the command - so the row asserting the name is absent published the name. It also defeated the tooling meant to remove it: a git filter-repo --replace-text pass matches a literal in reading order and does not match a bracket class, so a published tree built from that tip would still have carried it while the cleaning pass reported success. The pattern is now stored rot13-encoded with a rot13: prefix and decoded by Expand-LwgRptLiteral in bin/lwg-evidence.ps1 at the moment the argument array is built; the ENCODED form is what the detail line prints. Rot13 is a transposition and not secrecy, and the requirement it satisfies is exactly that no tracked file spells the target IN READING ORDER - so grep finds nothing because there is nothing to find, an automated replace pass is not silently defeated, and neither the file nor the rendered row hands the string to a reader. The -i flag stays dropped: the pattern is still the single source of the case-insensitivity. WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER: only the probe ARGUMENTS are held back from the rendered output. If git ever echoed the decoded pattern in an error message that text could reach a detail line through Get-LwgRptProcessWhy, truncated but not filtered; no path observed here produces that, which is an observation about this rule rather than a property of the mechanism. WORKING TREE ONLY, unchanged from the old rule. The plan additionally requires `git log -p --all` to be clean, which is a different and much larger claim about history that this row does not make, and the history scrub is deliberately NOT coupled to the identity rewrite in P3-identity - they are separate decisions with separate risks and either can be taken without the other. WHY THIS CAVEAT NO LONGER SPELLS THE REMOVED CONSTRUCTION'S REAL LETTERS, changed 2026-08-03 here and in the same illustration in bin/lwg-evidence.ps1 and tests/evidence_states.ps1. It used to quote the first three letters of the name that construction spelled. Three letters is not the name, and they are also the first three of the PUBLISHER's name, so quoting them disclosed nothing - the problem is that they matched the by-hand pre-publication sweep for that construction, which has no way to tell a prose example from a real obfuscated name. Three permanent hits that always need the same paragraph of explanation teach a reviewer to wave the sweep through, and that is how a real hit gets waved through beside them. No part of the argument depended on which letters were used, so the illustration was moved to letters that spell nothing. THIS CHANGED AN EXAMPLE AND NOT A RULE: the probe on this row is untouched, and the reading-order reduction in tests/evidence_states.ps1 that actually enforces the property is untouched, so nothing that was being checked stopped being checked

items.title: monitors/ feasibility spike - does a monitor receive rate-limit or cost data?
items.caveat: THE SPIKE RAN ON 2026-07-31 AND ITS VERDICT IS NEGATIVE. The old rule required monitors/monitors.json to exist, which meant it could only ever observe a POSITIVE outcome - and the plan explicitly permits a negative one, with both modules left declared unbuilt. So a spike that was run properly and correctly declined would have gone on reporting NOT STARTED forever, which is the rule mistaking an answer it did not like for an answer it never got. The row now points at the page that records the finding, and passes on either verdict, because what this item asks for is that the question be ANSWERED. A correctly-declined spike is a completion, and it has a date. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: that the verdict is correct. The reasoning is on the page and is reviewable there; this probe confirms the page exists and states a verdict

items.section: Phase B - Verbosity control that actually binds
items.title: lw-watchtower:verbose on|off, persisted in config.json as one verbosity setting shared with lw-watchtower:brief, delivered by an output style
items.caveat: THE PLAN'S OWN WORDING IS NOT WHAT WAS BUILT, and this item was rewritten to say what is rather than to keep a tick pointing at something else. The plan said 'bound per prompt', which means a UserPromptSubmit hook appending the rules to every prompt; a11f6f6 rejected exactly that for `brief` and `plain` and the same reasoning governs here - a hook registration cannot be made conditional, so the process is spawned on EVERY prompt whether the preference is on or off, at the 285 ms already recorded under mission_drift - one development machine's measurement of PowerShell 5.1 interpreter startup rather than a constant, and a slower machine pays more of it. So verbose ships the way its siblings do: bin/lwg-toggle.ps1 -Flag verbose records the preference in output_style.verbosity, and output-styles/lw-watchtower-verbose.md carries the behaviour. brief and verbose are ONE key with three values rather than two booleans, because a per-repo override is merged key by key and two booleans could have been set at different scopes with no writer present to stop them contradicting each other. WHAT IS NOT BUILT, stated rather than implied by the tick: nothing BINDS. An output style is advisory - it is appended to the system prompt at session start, no hook sits between the model and the transcript, and the section title's phrase 'that actually binds' is therefore still unsatisfied by this item and by the whole of Phase B. It also cannot be switched mid-session and does not reach subagents at all. On 30 July 2026, commands/brief.md and commands/verbose.md were merged into commands/verbosity.md; the evidence path above reflects that merge.

items.title: lw-watchtower:ask on|off with a Stop-hook decision gate that can block turn-end - CLOSED UNBUILT, THE COMMAND REMOVED

evidence.note: NOT DONE, AND NOT DOABLE. The command half shipped and the enforcement half never did; on 30 July 2026 the owner REMOVED the command half too - commands/ask.md, the interaction.ask key and the toggle's handling of it are all deleted - so there is nothing left to cite and this row renders unverified, which is the honest answer. It is deliberately NOT repointed at some surviving file to keep a tick: the probe used to name commands/ask.md and would have gone red on the deletion, and swapping in another path would have been manufacturing a pass for work that was never done. WHY IT CANNOT BE BUILT, so nobody re-attempts it: a Stop hook can refuse to end a turn, but by the time Stop fires the prose has already been printed, so it cannot stop a decision being scrolled past - which is the entire point of the item - and it has no way to detect a question that SHOULD have been asked and was not. The mechanism the title asks for does not exist at any hook event. The reasoning is kept in config.json under $removed_keys_comment and in docs/commands.md. The command name is written here WITHOUT a leading slash on purpose: bin/lwg-doctor.ps1 fails on a /lw-watchtower:<name> reference with no command file behind it.

items.title: lw-watchtower:ask-inline on|off - batch open decisions into one survey, 4 questions max - CLOSED UNBUILT, THE COMMAND REMOVED

The '4 questions max, 2-4 options each' shape was never a rule this plugin applied either: it is a platform limit on the question tool, enforced at that tool, and a plugin flag claiming credit for it would be counting someone else's constraint as its own coverage. items.title: Written proposal: role contract, extension path, one recommended design with trade-offs
items.caveat: THIS WAS `manual` UNTIL 2026-07-31, and the reason was real rather than procedural: the research lived in a plan file outside this repository, nothing tracked here carried the finding, and reading the plan's own tick as evidence would have been exactly the defect this plugin exists to catch. docs/roles.md now carries the contract, so the row is checkable and the old note's own instruction - 'land the proposal and this becomes checkable' - is what closed it. WHAT THE TICK PROVES IS THE PAGE AND THE HEADING, AND NOTHING MORE. It does not establish that the contract is well designed, that the extension path works, or that the trade-offs recorded against the recommended design are the right ones. The title asks for a written proposal; a file probe can confirm that something was written and where, and no probe here can review it

items.section: Research complete - findings and the resulting design
items.title: verification_gate classifies agents from an lw-class frontmatter key, not two literal name arrays
items.caveat: THE RULE WAS TIGHTENED ON 30 JULY 2026 RATHER THAN LEFT TO PASS ON A WORD. It used to be 'lib/stop_advisories.ps1 contains lw-class', and on that file the literal `lw-class` appears in COMMENTS and in one display label - so deleting the classifier outright and leaving the comments behind would have kept this item green. That is the same comment-satisfiable shape as the old P6-workflow-guard rule, in the same manifest, and it is fixed the same way: the probe now names the CALL SITE, Get-LwgAgentClassInfo -Name, which is the line that resolves an observed agent_type back to a role file and reads the key out of its frontmatter. The item did not change state - it passed before and passes now - so this is a strictly stronger rule over the same verdict. WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT PROVE: that the classifier returns the right answer. Nothing in this repository tests verification_gate, or any other observing module; the behaviour was confirmed by hand against 12 end-to-end runs through the real Stop hook when it landed, and nothing re-runs that. Note also that the plan asked for the two config.json name arrays to be DELETED and they were deliberately kept as a fallback - see PD-rename, which is where that decision bites.

items.section: Research complete - findings and the resulting design
items.title: doctor asserts zero verify-class roles installed while verification_gate is enabled
items.caveat: TIGHTENED ON 30 JULY 2026 for the same reason as PD-classification: the old rule was 'bin/lwg-doctor.ps1 contains lw-class', and every occurrence of that literal in that file is inside a comment or a detail string, so the check could have been deleted with the rule still green. It now requires the check to be REGISTERED - Invoke-Check -Id 'agent-roles' - and the assertion it exists for to still be spelled out after it. Passed before, passes now; strictly stronger, no state change. WHAT THE DOCTOR CHECK ITSELF PROVES, since that is what the tick rests on: with verification_gate enabled, ZERO installed verify-class roles is a FAIL, because the module can then nag and never clear. A role counts by its own lw-class: verify, or by a name in module_config.verification_gate.verify_agents THAT HAS A FILE ON DISK. It is a LOWER BOUND and says so - roles shipped by other plugins are not enumerable from here - so it can produce a spurious FAIL and never a false PASS. It is a WIRING check: it does not establish that the advisory fires, only that a role capable of disarming it exists.

items.title: hq-* to lw-* rename across config, stop_advisories, statusline and prose
items.caveat: FINISHED ON 31 JULY 2026, IN THE ONLY ORDER THAT WAS SAFE. blocked_by names PD-classification, which went DONE on 30 July 2026, so the sequencing constraint this section is about was satisfied first. THE SEQUENCE, because it is the substance of the item and not a formality: (1) the six role files in the owner's user-scope ~/.claude/agents were RENAMED from hq-* to lw-* and each was given an explicit lw-class - work for implementer, scribe and healer, verify for verifier, neutral for orchestrator and explorer - on the machine that holds them, which is OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY; (2) the classifier was run and observed resolving all six names to those classes from the user scope; (3) only then were the four names hq-implementer, hq-scribe, hq-healer and hq-verifier struck from config.json's module_config.verification_gate arrays and from the matching -Default arrays in lib/stop_advisories.ps1. Done in the other order, all six of those roles would have become unclassified at once - each returning the empty string, which means NO INFORMATION and never 'not a verifier' - so verification_gate would have stopped seeing that operator's work AND their verification, silently, while still counting toward the SessionStart banner's coverage number: the founding defect, reintroduced by finishing a rename. WHAT WAS KEPT: every generic name (implementer, scribe, engineer, healer, verifier, qa-agent, code-review, security-adversarial-review). Those have no role file at all, so they can never declare lw-class and the arrays are the only thing that can ever classify them. WHAT WAS REMOVED BEYOND THE NAMES, by explicit owner directive that no hq-* agent exists anywhere: the hq-healer.md compatibility probes in statusline/statusline.ps1 and bin/lwg-setup.ps1, and the (hq-)? alternation in the status line's orchestrator segment - which never matched the shipped lw-orchestrator and now does. THE CROSS-MACHINE CONSEQUENCE IS ACCEPTED, NOT OVERLOOKED: any other machine still carrying role files under the old spelling loses classification for them until it repeats the rename, and its health segment renders purple if its healer role is only there. This is recorded at config.json's $classifier_comment, in docs/roles.md and in CHANGELOG.md. WHAT THE PROBE PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: the four lw-* role files exist under agents/ AND config.json no longer contains the string "hq- anywhere, which is what makes the strike itself checkable rather than asserted. It does not prove the six USER-SCOPE files were renamed, because they live outside this tree and nothing here can read them; that half rests on the classifier output pasted into the commit. The manifest's evidence schema carries exactly ONE evidence object per item, so the config.json probe is folded in as a fifth path under the shared not_contains rather than written as a second entry.

items.title: /lw-watchtower:delegate on|off enforced by a PreToolUse gate, default off
items.caveat: THE PROBE PROVES REGISTRATION, NOT REFUSAL. It PARSES hooks/hooks.json and asserts that ONE PreToolUse entry invokes lib/gate_delegate.ps1 and that the SAME entry's matcher names all five tools this caveat lists below - which is the half that was missing for the whole of this item's history, since until 30 July 2026 this plugin registered no PreToolUse hook of any kind. THE RULE WAS A REGEX UNTIL 3 AUGUST 2026 AND IT BOUND NOTHING TOGETHER. It read `(?s)"PreToolUse".*"matcher"...".*gate_delegate\.ps1` over the raw text, where (?s) makes the dot span newlines and each .* runs greedily across the whole document - so it asserted three independent facts about one file rather than one fact about one entry. Measured: a hooks.json with an EMPTY PreToolUse array and this gate registered on PostToolUse satisfied it, and PostToolUse runs after the tool call has already executed, so the row attesting this plugin's only blocking component would have rendered DONE over a plugin that refuses nothing. It also read one tool name out of the matcher until 1 August 2026 and two after it, on a caveat naming five, so any narrowing that left the named ones standing was invisible. Widening the regex was rejected as the fix - matcher order is not fixed by anything and the fragments stay unbound however long the pattern gets - so the file is parsed instead, by a `hook` evidence kind that exists for this one question. It does NOT establish that the gate actually refuses a call, that it refuses the right callers, or that it fails safe: a registered hook that exits 0 on every path would pass this probe. What establishes THAT is tests/gate_delegate.ps1 - 93 cases through a real pipe into a real child process, run by the fast-checks job on every push and every PR. Confirmed to FAIL against a deliberately broken gate before being kept - with ONE NAMED EXCEPTION, because that sentence stopped being true of every case on 1 August 2026: the four cases added for the PowerShell tool passed against the pre-fix tree and could not have done otherwise, since the gate is tool-blind and the hole was in the matcher rather than in the gate. CORRECTED 2026-08-03, BECAUSE THE SENTENCE HERE NAMED TWO CASES THAT DO NOT GO RED AT THE BASELINE. It read: the cases that went red there are the registration case and M1. Neither half holds. At fd8d023 the PreToolUse array holds exactly ONE entry naming gate_delegate.ps1, so the registration case PASSES there; and hooks/hooks.json line 43 and tests/gate_delegate.ps1 line 147 both list the SAME four tools - Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash - so section A missing/surplus coverage case finds nothing missing and nothing surplus and passes there too. M1 does not exist at fd8d023 at all: the string GateMatcher occurs zero times in that file. A case that is not in the tree cannot have gone red in it. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is a narrower claim than the one that was made: M1 goes red only when it is INJECTED INTO A SNAPSHOT OF THE PRE-FIX TREE. That is a legitimate method and it is not the same thing as a case going red at the baseline, which is what this caveat asserted. HOW THIS WAS ESTABLISHED, said plainly because the distinction is the entire point of the correction: by reading hooks/hooks.json, tests/gate_delegate.ps1 and the GateMatcher occurrence count out of fd8d023 with git show - NOT by running the suite at that commit. No suite was run at fd8d023 to produce this note, so it is a claim about what those files contain and not about what a run reported. This is the same defect as the one tracked against the red-first note in tests/gate_delegate.ps1, and it survived the sweep for that one because this sentence omits the words in section A, which is the string that sweep keyed on. A deliberately slower probe running that suite here was rejected: it takes about half a minute, which is not a cost a report command should impose, and CI already runs it on every change. WHAT IS ENFORCED, PLAINLY, so this tick is not read as more than it is: with interaction.delegate on, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash and PowerShell are refused for any call that did not come from a subagent. PowerShell was NOT on that list until 1 August 2026, on a plugin that supports Windows and nothing else - so an armed gate could be walked round by asking for the other shell while this item ticked and /lw-watchtower:status printed the gate as live. The probe now requires BOTH names in the matcher, which is why it is worth more than it was; it still proves registration and not refusal. Nothing a subagent does is refused, and nothing checks that a dispatch was any good. It ships OFF, which is what the title asks for.

items.title: Evidence-backed checklist command with a fourth state for unverified
items.caveat: EVIDENCE REPLACED ON 2026-08-03, BECAUSE THE OLD RULE WAS COMMENT-SATISFIABLE - the third instance of that shape in this manifest and the one PE-sitrep's caveat predicted when it recorded that nobody had swept for it. It required a commit on main whose SUBJECT matched (?i)checklist, which any commit mentioning the word satisfies: a commit REMOVING the command satisfies it, and so does every one of this row's own corrections. The pattern was the bare feature name, so the row had been green by accident rather than on evidence for its whole life - every commit past v0.3.0 that touched this file carries the word. The rule now probes the three files the feature is made of; the former `progress` block WAS that probe and is deleted rather than left duplicating the evidence, exactly as PE-sitrep's was on 2026-07-31. THE SWEEP PE-SITREP ASKED FOR HAS NOW BEEN DONE, and it is recorded here because a sweep nobody records is a sweep the next reader repeats: two `kind: commit` rules remain, P0-ci-exit3 (match 'capability a skip blames') and P0-statedir (match 'state dir by discovery'), and both patterns are distinctive multi-word phrases from the work itself rather than a feature name, so neither is satisfied by a routine commit that merely mentions the subject. That is a weaker guarantee than a file probe and it is not nothing: a subject pattern is subject-satisfiable whatever it says, so those two rows still rest on somebody having written an accurate commit subject. WHAT THE TICK NOW PROVES, WHICH IS LESS THAN THE TITLE CLAIMS: commands/checklist.md, bin/lwg-checklist.ps1 and checklist.json all exist. Nothing reads any of them, so it does not prove the command runs, and it says nothing whatever about the fourth state - that UNVERIFIED is rendered, and rendered for the right inputs, is established by tests/evidence_states.ps1 and by nothing in this row.

items.title: Brief but complete sitrep that separates verified from reported and names what it could not determine
items.caveat: EVIDENCE REPLACED ON 2026-07-31, AFTER v0.3.0 WAS TAGGED, BECAUSE THE OLD RULE WAS COMMENT-SATISFIABLE. It required a commit on main whose SUBJECT matched (?i)sitrep, which any commit mentioning the word satisfies - including one that deleted the feature, and including this row's own corrections. That is the same rule shape this repository removed from P6-workflow-guard on 30 July 2026, and it survived here because nobody swept for the shape after fixing the one instance. The rule now probes for the two files the feature is made of. The former progress probe was that same file check and is deleted rather than left duplicating the evidence. WHAT THE TICK NOW PROVES, WHICH IS LESS THAN THE TITLE CLAIMS: commands/sitrep.md and bin/lwg-sitrep.ps1 both exist. Nothing reads either file, so it does not prove the command runs, and it says nothing about whether the report separates verified from reported or names what it could not determine - that is a judgement about output that no probe in this manifest makes

items.title: Guided install: per-section confirmation, diff before write, backup, rollback, never clobber
items.caveat: WHAT THE TICK PROVES, WHICH IS FAR LESS THAN THE TITLE CLAIMS: commands/setup.md and bin/lwg-setup.ps1 both exist. Neither `contains` nor `not_contains` is set, so nothing opens either file - Test-Path twice is the entire proof - and bin/lwg-setup.ps1 is about 1,700 lines. The title lists FIVE behavioural properties and this probe establishes NONE of them. THIS ROW CARRIED NO CAVEAT AT ALL UNTIL 2026-08-03, which made it the largest unqualified claim in the manifest: PE-sitrep has identical evidence over a REPORTING command and has carried this sentence since 31 July, while the row attesting that an installer is safe to point at a stranger's settings.json said nothing. WHERE EACH PROPERTY ACTUALLY STANDS, so a reader does not have to infer it from a tick: backup, rollback and part of never-clobber ARE exercised - tests/setup_merge.ps1 drives the installer's statusline and hooks sections through a real child process and asserts that unrelated keys survive, that one backup is taken, that the merge is idempotent and that a bad write rolls back. Per-section confirmation and diff-before-write are exercised by NOTHING, anywhere: they are interactive paths and no case reaches them. That suite is deliberately NOT cited as this row's evidence: it takes about half a minute, and PD-delegate's caveat already records why a report command does not run a suite of that cost - CI runs it on every push and every PR, which is where it belongs. So this row cites two paths and names, here, the suite that would establish three of the five. IT IS ALSO NOT A CLEAN BILL ON never-clobber: an open defect on this repository records the marketplace-detection probe reading a path that does not exist on a live install, so setup writes a duplicate hook registration with its own warning suppressed. That is exactly the property this row's title ticks, and no probe in this manifest can see it.

items.title: CI guard fails any workflow introducing self-hosted, pull_request_target or secrets usage
items.caveat: THE RULE WAS REPLACED ON 30 JULY 2026, AND THE OLD ONE WAS WORTHLESS. It read '.github/workflows/ci.yml contains the string self-hosted' - which A COMMENT SATISFIED, and which would have gone on passing while a self-hosted runner was actually introduced, because the string is present either way. It reported a verified protection and checked nothing, which is the precise defect this whole plugin exists to catch, sitting inside the plugin's own evidence manifest. The rule now RUNS tests/workflow_guard.ps1, which PARSES every file under .github/workflows/ into a tree and asks nine rules about structure rather than text. EXIT CODES, because 2 IS NOT A PASS: 0 no rule fired; 1 at least one hit OR at least one file that would not parse; 2 the guard ABORTED and nothing was established - an enumeration returning zero files is an abort, never an empty-set pass. Only 0 renders DONE here. Both 1 and 2 fall through to NOT STARTED with the observed exit code printed in the detail line, and nonzero_means:'unverified' is deliberately NOT set: that knob would launder a real violation (exit 1) into 'could not check', which is the opposite of what this item is for. WHAT A PASS STILL DOES NOT PROVE: it is a statement about the files in that ONE directory on THIS branch. An action pulled from another repository - uses: owner/repo@ref - runs code the guard never reads, digest pinning does not exist here, and workflows on other branches are not scanned. The guard's own allowlist is empty on purpose.

items.title: No self-hosted runner group is available to this repo at org level

evidence.note: runner-group visibility is an ORGANISATION setting. Reading it needs admin scope on the org, which this machine's gh token is not guaranteed to hold, and a 403 would be indistinguishable from 'no groups exist' - the two conclusions are opposite and the API answer is the same. Left unverified deliberately rather than probed and misreported. This is the highest-severity item on the whole plan and it is the one nothing here can check

items.title: Branch protection on main requiring the context 'Fast checks (JSON + PowerShell parse)' verbatim
items.caveat: THE REQUIRED CONTEXT IS A CHECK-RUN NAME, NOT A JOB ID, and this title said 'requiring fast-checks' until 3 August 2026 - which is the job id and is the string that will never report. GitHub matches a required status check by the check run's NAME, which for a job carrying a name: key is that display name: 'Fast checks (JSON + PowerShell parse)', capitalisation, spaces and parentheses exactly. Typing the id blocks every pull request forever, and the required-checks field takes free text and validates it against no workflow, so the mistake is silent. The gate-regression job was deleted from .github/workflows/ci.yml on 30 July 2026 with the destructive command gate; if any rule still names it - or its display name, 'Gate regression suite' - main is BLOCKED on a check that can never report. WHAT THIS PROBE CANNOT DO, and it is most of the item: it only asks whether a protection object EXISTS. It cannot see which contexts that object requires, so it cannot tell a correctly named context from a misspelled one, and it will render DONE the moment any protection exists whatever it requires. The evidence for the context being right is a throwaway pull request that goes green and becomes mergeable, and nothing in this repository can stand in for it. tests/doc_claims.ps1 does hold docs/testing.md's Branch protection section to the name derived from ci.yml, which is the page half and not the setting half.

items.title: CI passes on main so the required checks can be made mandatory
items.caveat: this is the NEWEST run on main only. It says nothing about whether the run before it passed, and nothing at all about any branch other than main

items.section: Phase 7 - Automated UAT (performed by the orchestrator, including UI/UX)
items.title: Written UAT report with a per-item verdict, from a throwaway profile, covering every command and the adversarial cases
Repository visibility flipped to public, with branch protection enabled immediately after
items.blocked_reason: Deferred by explicit owner decision on 2026-07-31: v0.3.0 was tagged and released without flipping visibility, and the flip is deliberately not part of that pass. Branch protection - which this item requires immediately after the flip - is not configurable on the current plan before it, and the API answers 403 until then; see P6-branch-protection. A FURTHER PRECONDITION WAS ADDED ON 2026-07-31, AFTER v0.3.0 WAS TAGGED, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DESCRIBED HERE: an unresolved identity exposure must be resolved before the flip rather than after it. THIS FIELD USED TO SPELL OUT WHERE THAT EXPOSURE IS AND HOW TO RETRIEVE IT - the ref, its tip commit and the number of commits involved - and it also asserted that the exposure reached no further than whoever could already read the repository, which would have become a false containment claim the moment the flip made this file public. checklist.json ships to every consumer and commands/checklist.md instructs the model to print this command output verbatim, so both sentences were rendered on strangers screens as findings about their own repository: one a map to the exposure, the other a reassurance that was about to stop being true. Both are gone; the exposure itself is unchanged and is tracked in the issue that owns it, addressed to the people who can act on it. The remedies are owner actions and nothing in this manifest can take or attest to any of them, which is why this row is DECLARED blocked rather than observed to be.

items.title: Tag v0.3.0 and publish a release with notes from CHANGELOG.md
items.caveat: PORTABILITY FIX COMPLETED 2026-07-31, AND THE RULE DID NOT CHANGE - the engine did. The first half was always covered: nonzero_means turns git failing outright - not a repo, git broken - into UNVERIFIED rather than 'the tag is absent'. The half this caveat used to carry as an open gap was the multi-laptop case, where `git tag -l` exits 0 with EMPTY stdout because the ref namespace was never fetched, and this row fell through to the stdout_match branch and rendered NOT STARTED. That needed a knob bin/lwg-evidence.ps1 did not have, and it now has it: a `command` rule that proves its item FROM stdout is UNVERIFIED when stdout is empty, because a pattern cannot be settled either way against output that does not exist. No manifest change was required for it, which is why the evidence line above is byte-identical to the one this caveat was first written against. WHAT IT COSTS, said plainly: this row can now render only DONE or UNVERIFIED, never NOT STARTED. A tag that was genuinely never cut produces exit 0 and empty stdout too, and is indistinguishable from a tag that was never fetched, so both read as 'could not tell'. That is the conservative direction on purpose - the alternative was a row that told a reader on a --no-tags clone that no release exists - but it does mean the absence of a release is a thing this row cannot report. Read a DONE here as 'the tag is present in THIS clone's ref namespace' and nothing more; it says nothing about the tag on the remote, and nothing about a release having been published from it
